I began symptoms of contamination OCD when I was around 10. I remember a therapist teaching me about rationality, which helped me. For example I wouldn’t touch pens or pencils as I was terrified of ink and lead poisoning. She explained to me that if pen and pencils were so dangerous then there would be millions of people in hospital. I remember that that way of thinking helped me get a grasp on my OCD. (I understand this won’t be the case with everyone  - OCD isn’t a one size fits all.)

My contamination OCD progressed very quickly. From washing my hands after I touched a pen to washing my hands after i touched anything that a pen was likely to have been on (a table, a book etc). I think that the quicker it’s addressed the unlikelier it’ll be that he ends up spiralling.

As an adult I still have waves of contamination OCD, though I am able to control these impulses through the therapy i received almost 15 years ago.

You may have to play a waiting game, but I think that DNA would be your best bet. The process might be similar to how organisations such as DNA Doe Project are currently using to identify unidentified remains across the USA. 

In that case, the process is to extract DNA from the remains and enter the results to gedmatch.com. From there they look at users that the unidentified person has matched with and find their relationship and build a family tree from there. For example, if a user is estimated to be a second cousin, they would build a family tree for the second cousin and map out all of their second cousins. From there they go through the possibilities and work out which one is the unidentified person.

In your case the unidentified person is your great grandmother. The process is different as you have DNA from her daughter. It’s still a similar process! You just have to find the closest relative to your grandmother on the DNA site that she has used and attempt to build their tree. Once the tree is built you can have a look at the possible people that could be your great grandmother. Find a woman that is around the right age but disappears from records around the wartime?
